blocks.text: 31 תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית 31
blocks.layout: header, page numbers both corners

blocks.text: נִשְׁמַת כָּל־חַי תְּבָרֵךְ אֶת־שִׁמְךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ. וְרוּחַ כָּל־בָּשָׂר תְּפָאֵר וּתְרוֹמֵם זִכְרְךָ מַלְכֵּנוּ תָּמִיד. מִן הָעוֹלָם וְעַד־הָעוֹלָם אַתָּה אֵל. וּמִבַּלְעָדֶיךָ אֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ גּוֹאֵל וּמוֹשִׁיעַ פּוֹדֶה וּמַצִּיל וּמְפַרְנֵס וּמְרַחֵם בְּכָל־עֵת צָרָה וְצוּקָה. אֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא אָתָּה:
blocks.layout: lines 1–5, full-width single column; first line indented

blocks.text: אֱלֹהֵי הָרִאשׁוֹנִים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִים. אֱלוֹהַּ כָּל־בְּרִיּוֹת. אֲדוֹן כָּל־תּוֹלָדוֹת. הַמְהֻלָּל בְּרֹב הַתִּשְׁבָּחוֹת. הַמְנַהֵג עוֹלָמוֹ בְּחֶסֶד וּבְרִיּוֹתָיו בְּרַחֲמִים. וַיְיָ לֹא־יָנוּם וְלֹא־יִישָׁן. הַמְעוֹרֵר יְשֵׁנִים וְהַמֵּקִיץ נִרְדָּמִים. וְהַמֵּשִׂיחַ אִלְּמִים. וְהַמַּתִּיר אֲסוּרִים וְהַסּוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים וְהַזּוֹקֵף כְּפוּפִים. לְךָ לְבַדְּךָ אֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים:
blocks.source_reference: allusions: Ps 121:4 (לֹא יָנוּם וְלֹא יִישָׁן); Ps 146:7–8 (מַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים … זֹקֵף כְּפוּפִים); Ps 145:14 (סוֹמֵךְ … לְכָל־הַנֹּפְלִים). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: lines 6–11; runs on without a paragraph break; לֹא־ ends line 8 with maqaf

blocks.text: אִלּוּ פִּינוּ מָלֵא שִׁירָה כַּיָּם וּלְשׁוֹנֵנוּ רִנָּה כַּהֲמוֹן גַּלָּיו וְשִׂפְתוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבַח כְּמֶרְחֲבֵי רָקִיעַ וְעֵינֵינוּ מְאִירוֹת כַּשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְכַיָּרֵחַ וְיָדֵינוּ פְרוּשׂוֹת כְּנִשְׁרֵי שָׁמָיִם וְרַגְלֵינוּ קַלּוֹת כָּאַיָּלוֹת. אֵין אֲנַחְנוּ מַסְפִּיקִים לְהוֹדוֹת לְךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ וּלְבָרֵךְ אֶת־שְׁמֶךָ. עַל־אַחַת מֵאָלֶף אֶלֶף אַלְפֵי אֲלָפִים וְרִבֵּי רְבָבוֹת פְּעָמִים הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁעָשִׂיתָ עִם־אֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְעִמָּנוּ: מִמִּצְרַיִם גְּאַלְתָּנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וּמִבֵּית עֲבָדִים פְּדִיתָנוּ. בְּרָעָב זַנְתָּנוּ וּבְשָׂבָע כִּלְכַּלְתָּנוּ. מֵחֶרֶב הִצַּלְתָּנוּ. וּמִדֶּבֶר מִלַּטְתָּנוּ. וּמֵחֳלָיִם רָעִים וְנֶאֱמָנִים דִּלִּיתָנוּ: עַד־הֵנָּה עֲזָרוּנוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ. וְלֹא־עֲזָבוּנוּ חֲסָדֶיךָ. וְאַל־תִּטְּשֵׁנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לָנֶצַח:
blocks.layout: starts mid-line 11 after מוֹדִים: and runs through mid-line 22

blocks.text: עַל־כֵּן אֵבָרִים שֶׁפִּלַּגְתָּ בָּנוּ. וְרוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּפַחְתָּ
blocks.layout: end of line 22 (עַל־ ends the line with maqaf) to line 23, the last line; continues on s94 with בְּאַפֵּינוּ

blocks.text: 31 Morning Prayer 31
blocks.layout: header

blocks.text: נשמת
blocks.layout: unpointed Hebrew cue at the start of line 1

blocks.text: Let the breath of all the living praise Thy Name, O Lord our God, and the spirit of all flesh glorify and exalt Thy memory, O our King, for ever. From eternity to eternity Thou art God and besides Thee we have no King, Redeemer, Helper, Deliverer, Liberator and Provider, nor one to show compassion at every time of trouble and distress. We have no King besides Thee,
blocks.layout: lines 1–7

blocks.text: O God of the first and the last, God of all creatures, Master of all generations, who is praised by an abundance of eulogies, who conducts His world with grace and His creatures with compassion. The Lord neither slumbers nor sleeps, He wakes sleepers and arouses slumberers, causes the dumb to speak, frees the bound, supports the falling and straightens the bent. We give thanks to Thee alone.
blocks.layout: lines 7–13; 'slum-/bers' line-wrap hyphen joined

blocks.text: Were our mouth as full of song as the sea and our tongue of exultation as the roar of the waves and our lips of praise as the expanse of the sky and our eyes as radiant as the sun and the moon and our hands spread out as wide as the eagles of heaven and our feet as swift as deer, we should still be unable to thank Thee enough, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, and to bless Thy Name for even one of the many thousands and myriads of acts of kindness which Thou hast done for our fathers and ourselves. From Egypt hast Thou redeemed us, O Lord our God, and from the house of slaves hast Thou freed us. Thou hast fed us in famine and preserved us in abundance, saved us from the sword, let us escape from plague and raised us from severe and persistent illnesses. Up to now have Thy mercies aided us and Thy kindnesses not forsaken us, do not abandon us, O Lord our God, for ever.
blocks.layout: lines 13–31

blocks.text: Therefore the limbs which Thou hast allotted us, the spirit and the soul which Thou hast breathed into
blocks.layout: lines 31–32; 'al-/lotted' line-wrap hyphen joined; continues on s94 with 'our nostrils'

blocks.text: 32 תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית 32
blocks.layout: header spanning both columns

blocks.text: בְּאַפֵּינוּ. וְלָשׁוֹן אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתָּ בְּפִינוּ. הֵן הֵם יוֹדוּ וִיבָרְכוּ וִישַׁבְּחוּ וִיפָאֲרוּ וִירוֹמֲמוּ וְיַעֲרִיצוּ וְיַקְדִּישׁוּ וְיַמְלִיכוּ אֶת־שִׁמְךָ מַלְכֵּנוּ:
blocks.layout: right column, lines 1–6

blocks.text: כִּי כָל־פֶּה לְךָ יוֹדֶה. וְכָל־לָשׁוֹן לְךָ תִשָּׁבַע. וְכָל־בֶּרֶךְ לְךָ תִכְרַע. וְכָל־קוֹמָה לְפָנֶיךָ תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה. וְכָל־לְבָבוֹת יִירָאוּךָ. וְכָל־קֶרֶב וּכְלָיוֹת יְזַמְּרוּ לִשְׁמֶךָ.
blocks.source_reference: allusion: Isa 45:23 (כִּי־לִי תִּכְרַע כָּל־בֶּרֶךְ תִּשָּׁבַע כָּל־לָשׁוֹן). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: right column, lines 7–13; וְכָל־ ends lines 7–11 with maqaf

blocks.text: כַּדָּבָר שֶׁכָּתוּב
blocks.layout: right column, start of line 14; formula introducing the quotation

blocks.text: כָּל עַצְמוֹתַי תֹּאמַרְנָה יְיָ מִי כָמוֹךָ. מַצִּיל עָנִי מֵחָזָק מִמֶּנּוּ וְעָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן מִגּוֹזְלוֹ:
blocks.source_reference: Ps 35:10 (canonical: כָּל עַצְמוֹתַי תֹּאמַרְנָה יְהוָה מִי כָמוֹךָ מַצִּיל עָנִי מֵחָזָק מִמֶּנּוּ וְעָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן מִגֹּזְלוֹ). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: right column, lines 14–17

blocks.text: מִי יִדְמֶה־לָּךְ וּמִי יִשְׁוֶה־לָּךְ וּמִי יַעֲרָךְ־לָךְ. הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֵל עֶלְיוֹן קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ:
blocks.source_reference: allusions: Ps 89:7; Deut 10:17 (הָאֵל הַגָּדֹל הַגִּבֹּר וְהַנּוֹרָא); Gen 14:19 (אֵל עֶלְיוֹן קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: right column, lines 17–21

blocks.text: נְהַלֶּלְךָ וּנְשַׁבֵּחֲךָ וּנְפָאֶרְךָ וּנְבָרֵךְ אֶת־שֵׁם קָדְשֶׁךָ. כָּאָמוּר
blocks.layout: right column, lines 21–23

blocks.text: לְדָוִד בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת־יְיָ וְכָל־קְרָבַי אֶת־שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ:
blocks.source_reference: Ps 103:1 (canonical: לְדָוִד בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָה וְכָל־קְרָבַי אֶת־שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: right column, lines 24–25 (last lines)

blocks.text: our nostrils, and the tongue which Thou hast placed in our mouth, shall thank, bless, praise, extol, exalt, revere, sanctify and pay homage to Thy Name, O our King.
blocks.layout: left column, lines 1–6

blocks.text: For every mouth shall thank Thee, every tongue swear to Thee, every knee bend to Thee, every upright form bow down before Thee, all hearts shall fear Thee, all inwards and kidneys shall sing to Thy Name,
blocks.layout: left column, lines 6–13

blocks.text: according to the word which is written:
blocks.layout: left column, lines 13–14

blocks.text: ‘all my limbs say, O Lord, who is like Thee’. Thou deliverest the poor from him who is stronger than he, the poor and needy from him who would rob him.
blocks.layout: left column, lines 14–19; the printed quotation marks close after 'Thee' only

blocks.text: Who is like Thee, who resembles Thee, who can compare with Thee, O great, strong and awe-inspiring God, Supreme God, owner of heaven and earth.
blocks.layout: left column, lines 19–24; 'awe-in-/spiring': only the line-wrap hyphen is joined and the real compound hyphen is kept

blocks.text: Let us praise Thee, extol Thee and glorify Thee and bless Thy holy Name, as it is said:
blocks.layout: left column, lines 25–28; 'bless' is printed with a damaged glyph (looks like 'ble;s')

blocks.text: ‘By David. Let my soul praise the Lord and all my inwards His holy Name.
blocks.layout: left column, lines 28–30; no closing quotation mark is printed

blocks.text: 33 יוֹצֵר לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה. 33
blocks.layout: header spanning both columns, ends with a period

blocks.text: הָאֵל בְּתַעֲצֻמוֹת עֻזֶּךָ: הַגָּדוֹל בִּכְבוֹד שְׁמֶךָ: הַגִּבּוֹר לָנֶצַח וְהַנּוֹרָא בְּנוֹרְאוֹתֶיךָ:
blocks.layout: right column, lines 1–3, ordinary text size

blocks.text: הַמֶּלֶךְ:
blocks.layout: right column, centred on its own line in very large display type (about 3–4× body size). Typographic emphasis on a spoken word, not a heading. Paired with 'O King' in the English

blocks.text: יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רָם וְנִשָּׂא:
blocks.source_reference: allusion: Isa 6:1 (יֹשֵׁב עַל־כִּסֵּא רָם וְנִשָּׂא). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: right column, line after הַמֶּלֶךְ

blocks.text: שׁוֹכֵן עַד מָרוֹם וְקָדוֹשׁ שְׁמוֹ. וְכָתוּב
blocks.source_reference: allusion: Isa 57:15 (שֹׁכֵן עַד וְקָדוֹשׁ שְׁמוֹ מָרוֹם). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: right column, new paragraph with indent

blocks.text: רַנְּנוּ צַדִּיקִים בַּייָ לַיְשָׁרִים נָאוָה תְהִלָּה:
blocks.source_reference: Ps 33:1 (canonical: רַנְּנוּ צַדִּיקִים בַּיהוָה לַיְשָׁרִים נָאוָה תְהִלָּה). No printed citation.
blocks.layout: right column, end of line 2 of the paragraph to line 3

blocks.text: בְּפִי יְשָׁרִים תִּתְרוֹמָם: וּבְדִבְרֵי צַדִּיקִים תִּתְבָּרַךְ: וּבִלְשׁוֹן חֲסִידִים תִּתְקַדָּשׁ: וּבְקֶרֶב קְדוֹשִׁים תִּתְהַלָּל:
blocks.layout: right column, four lines, one stich per line; the first is indented. In יְשָׁרִים the sheva is printed low, well below the yod

blocks.text: וּבְמַקְהֲלוֹת רִבְבוֹת עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּרִנָּה יִתְפָּאַר שִׁמְךָ מַלְכֵּנוּ בְּכָל־דּוֹר וָדוֹר.
blocks.layout: right column, new indented paragraph, 3 lines

blocks.text: שֶׁכֵּן חוֹבַת כָּל־הַיְצוּרִים לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ לְהוֹדוֹת לְהַלֵּל לְשַׁבֵּחַ לְפָאֵר לְרוֹמֵם לְהַדֵּר לְבָרֵךְ לְעַלֵּה וּלְקַלֵּס עַל כָּל־דִּבְרֵי שִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבְּחוֹת דָּוִד בֶּן־יִשַׁי עַבְדְּךָ מְשִׁיחֶךָ:
blocks.layout: right column, last 7 lines, no paragraph break; כָּל־ ends a line with maqaf

blocks.text: O God, in the strength of Thy power, great in the glory of Thy Name, strong to eternity, awe-inspiring through Thy awesome deeds,
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 1, indented; 'eter-/nity' joined

blocks.text: O King
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 2 opening, ordinary type (no display emphasis)

blocks.text: seated on a throne high and exalted.
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 2, continuing the same sentence as 'O King'

blocks.text: שוכן
blocks.layout: unpointed Hebrew cue at the start of paragraph 3

blocks.text: He who everlasting dwells, exalted and holy is His Name as it is written:
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 3

blocks.text: Rejoice, O righteous ones, in the Lord, the offering of praise is becoming to the upright.
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 3 continued; no quotation marks

blocks.text: Through the mouth of the upright art Thou exalted and through the words of the righteous art Thou blessed, and through the tongue of the pious art Thou sanctified and in the midst of the saints art Thou extolled.
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 4, indented

blocks.text: ובמקהלות
blocks.layout: unpointed Hebrew cue at the start of paragraph 5

blocks.text: And through the throngs of the myriads of Thy people the House of Israel is Thy Name, O our King, glorified with joy in every generation.
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 5; 'glo-/rified' and 'gen-/eration' joined

blocks.text: For thus it is the duty of all creatures before Thee, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, to thank, to extol, to praise, to glorify, to exalt, to honour, to bless, to elevate and to sing praises with all the words of the songs and eulogies of David the son of Jesse, Thy servant, Thine anointed.
blocks.layout: left column, paragraph 5 continued to the end of the column

blocks.text: 34 יוֹצֵר לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 34
blocks.layout: header, no final period

blocks.text: יִשְׁתַּבַּח שִׁמְךָ לָעַד מַלְכֵּנוּ הָאֵל הַמֶּלֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ. כִּי לְךָ נָאֶה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שִׁיר וּשְׁבָחָה הַלֵּל וְזִמְרָה עֹז וּמֶמְשָׁלָה נֶצַח גְּדֻלָּה וּגְבוּרָה תְּהִלָּה וְתִפְאֶרֶת קְדֻשָּׁה וּמַלְכוּת בְּרָכוֹת וְהוֹדָאוֹת מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם:
blocks.layout: lines 1–5, full width

blocks.text: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֵל מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל בַּתִּשְׁבָּחוֹת אֵל הַהוֹדָאוֹת אֲדוֹן הַנִּפְלָאוֹת הַבּוֹחֵר בְּשִׁירֵי זִמְרָה מֶלֶךְ אֵל חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים:

blocks.text: 34 Morning Prayer for the New Year 34
blocks.layout: header

blocks.text: ישתבח
blocks.layout: unpointed Hebrew cue at the start of line 1

blocks.text: May Thy Name be praised for ever, O our King, God the great and holy King in heaven and on earth. For Thine, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, are song and glory, praise and music, might and dominion, victory, greatness and strength, fame and splendour, blessings and thanks from now until eternity.
blocks.layout: lines 1–6; 'great-/ness' joined

blocks.text: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, King famed in eulogies, God of thanksgiving, Master of wonders, who chooses songs of praise, O King, everlasting God.
blocks.layout: lines 6–8. The scope stops here, before the italic 'The reader recites half Kaddish.'

uncertainties.mark: The point under the alef looks like qamats (pausal form), not patah. Compare the earlier אַתָּה אֵל on line 3, which has patah.
Can't tell for sure whether the pe has a dagesh.
The dot in the yod (dagesh) is faint.
Hataf qamats under the het is likely but blurred.
Dagesh in the tet is uncertain.
Read as segol under the mem (the שְׁמֶךָ form), not שִׁמְךָ.
The first mem seems to carry hataf patah rather than plain sheva.
Printed with full vav (holam male), which differs from the canonical defective מִגֹּזְלוֹ. Read as printed.
Can't confirm a dagesh in either lamed.
Divine Name with the prefix: bet with patah, then a double yod with qamats under the second yod. I can't see a sheva under the first yod.
Can't confirm a dagesh in the shin.
The final 't' is damaged and looks like 'r'. I took this as a type defect, not a different word.
The second 's' is damaged and looks like ';'.

observations: The crops are safe. The bands cut the running-head line, but the full pages show it complete, and no body-text letters or points are cut anywhere.

Page breaks fall in matching places in both languages. Hebrew s92 ends at שֶׁנָּפַחְתָּ and s94 picks up at בְּאַפֵּינוּ; English s93 ends at 'breathed into' and s94 picks up at 'our nostrils'. Both fragments are kept under the same key, nishmat/al_ken.
On s94 and s95 each column covers the same text from top to bottom: both page-32 columns end with Ps 103:1, and both page-33 columns end with 'Thine anointed' / מְשִׁיחֶךָ.

הַמֶּלֶךְ on s95 is set in large display type, but it is a spoken word in the prayer and is kept as its own prayer_part. The English does not set it apart: 'O King seated on a throne…' runs as one ordinary sentence.
None of these pages prints a citation. Every verse reference given above is mine.
The Divine Name always appears as יְיָ, and as בַּייָ with the prefix.
Text after Yishtabach (the half-Kaddish rubric, וְעַתָּה יִגְדַּל־נָא, Kaddish, Barekhu, Yotzer) is left out, as the scope requires.
